subject: Request: evidence export patterns & SIEM handoff for on-prem Redwood deployment
messages:

Subject: Request: evidence export patterns for on-prem Redwood deployment

Hi team,

Thanks for the quick sync yesterday. Per our compliance review, HarborBank (ops+audit@harborbank.com) needs a short, auditable description of how Redwood will:

- Export evidence (logs, traces, metrics) from an air-gapped on-prem/private deployment into the bank's SIEM
- Ensure chain-of-custody and tamper-evidence for exported bundles
- Provide trace correlation hooks for their distributed transactions

Can you send a single-page summary + a minimal runbook sample (what we run during handoff) that covers: transport (syslog vs HEC), auth (mTLS, token rotation), retention & redaction, and acceptance test steps?

Attached: evidence-schema.xlsx (stub) — a matrix the audit team started.

Thanks,
Jordan

AcmeCloud

Subject: Re: Request: evidence export patterns for on-prem Redwood deployment

Jordan — thanks for outlining the asks. Attaching a short draft runbook and a one-pager we can use for compliance review. High level notes below, and a proposed handoff cadence.

Summary (short):
- Transport: prefer Splunk HEC over plain syslog for authenticated delivery and per-batch acknowledgements. Fallback: syslog TLS for legacy stacks.
- Auth: mutual TLS (server cert + client cert) for the on-prem forwarder; short-lived HEC tokens rotated by the customer's KMS every 7 days (customer-managed keys).
- Retention/scrub: Export bundles include raw logs + trace index. PII fields are redacted at the forwarder using configurable scrub rules; audit copy kept for 30 days in an immutable bucket (signed manifests).
- Trace hooks: Redwood will inject a correlation-id header (X-RW-CID) at request ingress and preserve it through LRUs; traces exported to SIEM include that id to allow joins with application traces.

Handoff cadence (proposed):
1) Pre-handoff review (we provide runbook draft and sample HEC config) — this week
2) Dry-run: forwarder -> partner staging HEC, observe ACKs and manifest signing — 2 days
3) Acceptance: audit validates manifests, checks scrub rules, signs off — 1 day
4) Production handover: scheduled maintenance window, final key exchange

I've attached runbook-draft.md. If this looks good I'll convert the one-pager into the format HarborBank needs.

—Ethan
Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Ethan/Jordan — adding a few technical constraints and sample config suggestions from the runtime side. Forwarding key considerations below.

On Tue, Dec 9, 2025 at 11:02 AM Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Jordan — thanks for outlining the asks. Attaching a short draft runbook and a one-pager we can use for compliance review. High level notes below, and a proposed handoff cadence.

Technical notes (runtime & forwarder):
- Batching/ordering: our forwarder guarantees per-shard ordering. For SIEM ingestion you should expect event bundles with a manifest.json listing checksums; we sign manifests with the customer-provided HSM key.
- Sampling: default sampling is 1% for debug-level traces to cap egress. For audited flows we recommend getting full traces for transactions that touch payment endpoints (configurable filter rules).
- Tracehook placement: Redwood will expose a lightweight tracehook library that instruments the API gateway and the worker pool. Hooks will emit X-RW-CID and a trace span id compatible with OpenTelemetry. We recommend setting max-span depth to limit export volume.
- Scrubbing and schema: redaction rules are applied at the forwarder; we support regex and json-path rules. Keep a redaction whitelist for fields required by audit (e.g., transaction_id).
- Transport security: Splunk HEC over mTLS + token is preferred. If customers require air-gap handoff, we support signed tarball export with SHA256 manifests and a signed transfer via SFTP to an approved DMZ.

Sample config excerpt (Splunk HEC):
-- splunk-hec-config.json (stub) --
{
  "hec_endpoint": "https://siem-acme.example.com:8088",
  "auth": {
    "client_cert_path": "/etc/forwarder/certs/client.pem",
    "ca_bundle": "/etc/forwarder/certs/ca.pem"
  },
  "bundling": {
    "max_events": 5000,
    "max_bytes": 5242880
  }
}

(We'll provide a full JSON config with example regex rules once the audit group shares their required fields.)

Kimberly Park
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
